advancement.createmetallurgy.foundry_bas: Craft a Foundry Basin and Foundry Lid
block.createmetallurgy.light_bulb.toolti: Emits _light_ based on the _Redstone_ signal received, and can link with other bulbs to form a _network_
block.createmetallurgy.mechanical_grinde: Uses _Rotational Power_ to grind anything placed on top — even _you_ and your _armor_!
createmetallurgy.ponder.casting_blocks.t: Casting blocks are used to cool molten metal into specific shapes
The Casting Basin is used to cast full blocks
While the Casting Table uses Graphite Molds to cast individual items
If using a funnel for output instead of doing it manually...
...a Brass Funnel may be needed to prevent the mold from being ejected
createmetallurgy.ponder.foundry_basin.he: Smelting Metals in the Foundry Basin
createmetallurgy.ponder.foundry_basin.te: The Foundry Basin works similarly to a Mixing Basin...
...however, it can only hold 9 items of the same type
Place a Foundry Lid on top to complete the foundry!
Just like a Mixing Basin, an output spout can extract recipe output...
...or drain fluids into a fluid tank
Make sure the foundry top is closed, otherwise no recipes will process
createmetallurgy.ponder.foundry_mixer.te: The Foundry Mixer works similarly to a Mechanical Mixer...
...however, it has a higher stress impact
Place a Glassed Foundry Lid between the two to enable alloying
To keep the molten metal at temperature...
Make sure the foundry top is closed, otherwise no recipes will process
If using fluid pipes instead of a fluid tank for output...
...a Smart Fluid Pipe may be needed to prevent pumping out unprocessed fluids
createmetallurgy.ponder.light_bulbs.text: Light Bulbs are an alternative light source to Redstone Lamps
Their brightness depends on the strength of the Redstone signal received
Light Bulbs can be dyed in any color
Place an item in the slot to link other bulbs into the same network
block.createmetallurgy.faucet.tooltip.su: Transfers fluids vertically downward to the block below — up to 5 blocks!
createmetallurgy.crucible.title: Crucible Info:
createmetallurgy.ponder.foundry.text_1: Industrial Crucibles can be used to build a multiblock foundry
createmetallurgy.ponder.foundry.text_2: ...you can use a Wrench to remove an installed Foundry Unit
createmetallurgy.ponder.foundry.text_3: You need to heat the foundry to smelt metals...
createmetallurgy.ponder.foundry.text_4: ...the foundry can be up to 5x5 in width to reach maximum temperature
createmetallurgy.ponder.foundry.text_5: However, each base block without a burner will cool the foundry down. The higher the temperature, the faster metals melt.
createmetallurgy.ponder.foundry.text_6: Unlike the Foundry Basin, the multiblock foundry is large enough to smelt bigger stacks and multiple item types simultaneously.
createmetallurgy.ponder.foundry.text_7: Wear Engineer's Goggles to see the foundry's current status. Temperature is displayed in Thermal Units (Tu).
createmetallurgy.ponder.foundry.text_8: Like an Item Vault, each face can be used for item input or output
createmetallurgy.ponder.foundry.text_9: The foundry can process all melting and alloying recipes from the Foundry Basin, plus its own high-temperature smelting recipes, alloy recipes, and entity melting recipes.
createmetallurgy.ponder.industrial_cruci: You can use a Wrench to add an observation window!
Multiple fluid types can be stored in the crucible simultaneously!
